title: A clock-aligned version of the zodiac label test, with no rotation left free: labels at the same clock position on different signs do not match (2 exact agreements in 2415 comparisons against 4.1 expected)
statement: The earlier tests of whether the zodiac figure labels repeat from sign to sign (P-L4-007, P-L4-010) had to search over rotations, because the order of the labels in a ring was taken from the transcription's line order. The pinned Zandbergen-Landini file gives more than order: every figure label on the twelve zodiac pages carries the clock position of its figure. That allows a test with a single alignment fixed in advance by the page itself: if the figures stood for a fixed series tied to position in the wheel (days or degrees counted from a common point), the label at a given clock position on one sign should recur at the same clock position on another. Method, public pages only, one transliteration: the 21 rings and rows of figure labels on the twelve zodiac pages that hold seven or more labels (ring sizes 19 and 10; 10 on each of four pages; 15 and 9; 12, 11 and 7; 18 and 12 twice; 20 and 10; 16 and 10 twice; the five-label inner rings and the short top rows are left out); for every pair of rings on different pages and every label of the first, the label of the second whose clock position is nearest; first word of the label only, uncertain readings taken at their first alternative. Null: the second ring turned by a random angle, 400 times. Result: 2 exact agreements in 2415 comparisons against a null mean of 4.1 (p = 0.94); within one glyph, 37 against 33.7 (p = 0.27). So with the alignment fixed by the page and no freedom to rotate, labels at the same place in the wheel do not agree across signs any more than labels at random places do, which removes the one loophole the rotation-searching tests left (that their correction for searching hid a true alignment). It agrees with both earlier results. Limits: I pooled every pair of rings, so outer rings are also compared with inner ones, which a roster split by ring would not predict to match and which dilutes any effect confined to same-ring pairs; clock positions in the file are given to the nearest quarter or half hour, coarser than the spacing of figures in the larger rings, so nearest-position pairing is off by a figure fairly often and an exact positional roster could be blurred by that; rings differ in size, so the same clock position is not the same ordinal; one transliteration. A same-ring-only run and a run by ordinal from a common starting clock position are the obvious next variants and should be declared before they are run.
check: From data/raw/ZL3b-n.txt take every zodiac figure label (unit Lz) with its first clock marker; group by page and by the label block it stands in; keep groups of seven or more; pair labels across pages by nearest clock position and count exact and one-glyph agreements against the second ring turned by a random angle. The claim fails if the same-ring-only variant, declared in advance, gives exact agreements at p below 0.01.
